title: This Bridge Isn't Collapsing... It Sinks on Purpose
script: This bridge isn't collapsing. It's sinking on purpose! In Greece, at the Corinth Canal, the road dives under the water so ships can sail right over it. Then it rises back up, and the cars drive on.

voice.instructions: Energetic, amazed YouTube Shorts narrator. Fast, punchy pace. Hit 'isn't collapsing' and 'on purpose' hard, playful disbelief, smile in the voice.

shots.image_prompt_full: Photorealistic vertical shot from the roadside at the very edge of a narrow single-lane steel road bridge lying flat at water level across a narrow canal of clear turquoise sea water, grey asphalt deck with a yellow center line and low steel railings, towering pale limestone canal walls behind. The bridge deck is ALREADY HALF UNDERWATER: sea water is rushing over the asphalt from both sides, foaming around the yellow center line, the steel railings are going under. In the foreground a red-and-white road barrier is down and a small white car and a man on a scooter have stopped right at the edge, people holding up phones in shock. Behind the sinking bridge, the tall white bow of a cruise ship is approaching down the canal. Bright Greek summer sunshine, realistic smartphone video look, no text, no watermark.
shots.end_image_prompt_full: Same camera position, same barrier, car, scooter and people: the bridge has now COMPLETELY DISAPPEARED under the turquoise water. Only ripples and a faint yellow line visible deep below the surface where the road was. The white bow of the cruise ship is now much closer, filling the upper half of the frame as it enters the spot. Bright Greek summer sunshine, realistic smartphone video look, no text, no watermark.
shots.motion_prompt: The whole road bridge deck sinks steadily straight down into the canal. Water rushes over the asphalt from both sides and swallows the railings, waves ripple outward. The people behind the barrier lean forward and film with their phones. The cruise ship keeps gliding closer. Realistic water physics, no collapse, no explosion, the bridge stays intact as it goes under.
